notes: Canonical memory-comparison SQL/data/parameters and batch counts; diagnostic, not a cross-core benchmark.
All timing precedes tracing. Allocation tracing disables GC for one query at a time; traced time is never reported.
Core allocation sites exclude Ruby internal objects. Answer digests compare query and execute paths on the first parameter.

results.sql: SELECT score FROM items WHERE id = $1
SELECT a.label, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY b.id LIMIT 1
SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id < $1 AND b.id < $1 AND c.id < $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id % 10 JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id < 10 AND c.id < 10 ORDER BY a.id

SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label, d.bucket FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id JOIN items d ON d.id = c.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 AND d.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id LEFT JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id AND c.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id,b.id FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.bucket=a.bucket AND abs(b.score-a.score)<50 WHERE a.id<$1 AND b.id<$1 ORDER BY a.id,b.id
SELECT a.id,b.id FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id=a.id AND length(b.label)>=4 WHERE a.id=$1 AND b.id=$1 ORDER BY a.id,b.id
SELECT a.id,lower(b.label) FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id=a.id WHERE a.id=$1 AND b.id=$1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id,abs(b.score-a.score) FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id=a.id WHERE a.id=$1 AND b.id=$1 AND abs(b.score)>=0 ORDER BY abs(a.id)
